text:
In Europe, **“select service” is used broadly** to include economy, limited-service, focused-service and lean-lifestyle hotels. A practical new-build brand longlist would usually include the following:

| Segment | Brands commonly considered | Typical fit |
|---|---|---|
| **Economy/value** | **ibis budget, ibis, ibis Styles, greet** | City centers, airports, business parks, roadside and secondary cities; Accor has an especially deep European distribution platform. ([group.accor.com](https://group.accor.com/en/documents-publications?utm_source=openai)) |
|  | **Holiday Inn Express** | One of the standard benchmarks for branded limited-service development throughout Europe. ([ihgplc.com](https://www.ihgplc.com/our-brands/holiday-inn-express?utm_source=openai)) |
|  | **Hampton by Hilton** | Strong focused-service candidate for urban, airport and regional markets. Hampton and Hilton Garden Inn have historically represented a substantial portion of Hilton’s European pipeline. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/emea/releases/hilton-continues-european-growth-with-6-new-sites?utm_source=openai)) |
|  | **B&B HOTELS** | Major European value brand, particularly relevant in France, Germany, Italy, Iberia and Central Europe. ([bbhotels-group.com](https://bbhotels-group.com/our-group/?utm_source=openai)) |
|  | **Premier Inn** | Particularly important in the UK and Germany; generally considered in lease/operator-led developments rather than as a conventional franchise option. ([premierinn.com](https://www.premierinn.com/gb/en/business/international-development.html?utm_source=openai)) |
|  | **Première Classe** | Primarily relevant in France and selected Continental European markets. ([corporate.louvrehotels.com](https://corporate.louvrehotels.com/en-us/our-brands/?utm_source=openai)) |
|  | **Scandic Go** | Increasingly relevant for economy projects in the Nordic countries, including both new construction and conversions. ([scandichotelsgroup.com](https://www.scandichotelsgroup.com/media/press-releases/2026/scandic-to-open-an-underground-hotel-in-stockholm-city-center/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Midscale/focused service** | **Hilton Garden Inn** | Upper-midscale focused-service product, generally with more F&B and meeting space than Hampton. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/emea/releases/hilton-continues-european-growth-with-6-new-sites?utm_source=openai)) |
|  | **Courtyard by Marriott** | Established upper-midscale select-service option for business districts, airports and mixed-use schemes. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/select-brands?utm_source=openai)) |
|  | **AC Hotels by Marriott** | Design-oriented select-service brand commonly evaluated for urban European locations. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/select-brands?utm_source=openai)) |
|  | **Hyatt Place** | Select-service option for airports, city centers and mixed-use projects; Hyatt has used both franchise and management structures in Europe. ([newsroom.hyatt.com](https://newsroom.hyatt.com/european_growth?utm_source=openai)) |
|  | **Park Inn by Radisson** | Cost-conscious midscale model intended to require lower capital investment than traditional full-service products. ([radissonhotels.com](https://www.radissonhotels.com/en-us/corporate/development-opportunities/our-brands?utm_source=openai)) |
|  | **Campanile / Kyriad** | Frequently considered in France, Benelux and parts of Central and Eastern Europe, especially for three-star midscale projects. ([corporate.louvrehotels.com](https://corporate.louvrehotels.com/en-us/our-brands/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Lean lifestyle/select service** | **Moxy Hotels** | One of Europe’s most established lifestyle-select concepts, with compact rooms, active public space and a relatively efficient operating model. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/select-brands?utm_source=openai)) |
|  | **Motto by Hilton** | Urban micro-hotel format suited to high-cost, central locations and adaptable to new build, conversion or adaptive reuse. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/emea/releases/motto-by-hilton-to-make-european-debut-in-rotterdam?utm_source=openai)) |
|  | **Ruby Hotels** | Space-efficient “urban micro”/lean-luxury concept, now owned by IHG; suitable for new builds, conversions and office reuse. ([ihgplc.com](https://www.ihgplc.com/en/news-and-media/news-releases/2025/ihg-hotels-and-resorts-acquires-ruby-its-20th-brand-and-targets-global-expansion?utm_source=openai)) |
|  | **Radisson RED** | Upscale lifestyle-select option with simplified service and a relatively efficient operating model. ([radissonhotels.com](https://www.radissonhotels.com/en-us/corporate/development-opportunities/our-brands?utm_source=openai)) |
|  | **Prize by Radisson** | Affordable design-led midscale brand, particularly relevant in Germany, Austria, Poland and selected UK/Ireland markets. ([radissonhotels.com](https://www.radissonhotels.com/en-us/corporate/media/press-releases/rhg-pphe-acceleration-growth-artotel?utm_source=openai)) |
|  | **Motel One / The Cloud One** | Major European “affordable design” competitor for prime urban sites; frequently uses leases, ownership or operator-led structures rather than conventional franchising. ([motel-one.com](https://www.motel-one.com/en/corporate/development/?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Extended-stay adjacency** | **Hyatt House, Residence Inn by Marriott, Element, Adagio** | Often evaluated alongside select-service brands where corporate, relocation or longer-stay demand is material. Hyatt Place/Hyatt House dual-brand projects can share facilities and operating infrastructure. ([newsroom.hyatt.com](https://newsroom.hyatt.com/news-releases?item=123661&utm_source=openai)) |

### Most common initial shortlist

For a conventional European new build, the names most likely to appear in an early feasibility or operator-selection exercise are:

1. **Holiday Inn Express**
2. **Hampton by Hilton**
3. **ibis / ibis Styles / ibis budget**
4. **Moxy**
5. **Hilton Garden Inn**
6. **Courtyard or AC Hotels**
7. **B&B HOTELS**
8. **Park Inn by Radisson or Prize by Radisson**
9. **Motel One**
10. **Premier Inn**, depending on country and deal structure

Brands such as **Garner** and **Four Points Flex by Sheraton** may also enter the discussion, but their positioning is currently more conversion-oriented, so they are generally less obvious first choices for a ground-up development. ([ihgplc.com](https://www.ihgplc.com/en/news-and-media/news-releases/2025/ihg-hotels-and-resorts-conversion-friendly-brands-fuel-growth-opportunities-for-owners?utm_source=openai))

The appropriate shortlist ultimately depends heavily on **country, room count, location type, target ADR, F&B requirements, franchise versus lease preference, territorial availability and brand-mandated construction cost per key**. Regional operators can be more competitive than global brands in markets such as the UK, France, Germany and the Nordics.
